'''Watkins:''' {{legend0|#e6e6e6|30–40%}} {{legend0|#d3d3d3|40–50%}} {{legend0|#b0b0b0|50–60%}} {{legend0|#7e7e7e|60–70%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[David Walters]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Frank Keating]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | turnout = 42% {{increase}} 9.19 [[percentage point|pp]] }} {{ElectionsOK}} The '''1994 Oklahoma gubernatorial election''' was held on November 8, 1994, and was a race for [[Governor of Oklahoma]]. Former [[United States Associate Attorney General]] [[Frank Keating]] pulled an upset in the three-way race to become only the third [[Republican Party of Oklahoma|Republican]] governor in Oklahoma history. The Democratic vote was split between [[Lieutenant Governor of Oklahoma|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Jack Mildren]], an [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]] star quarterback from 1969 to 1971, and former Democratic congressman [[Wes Watkins]], who ran as an independent. Watkins won 24% of the vote and carried numerous counties (by wide margins in some cases); his 233,000 votes far exceeded Keating's 171,000-vote winning margin over Mildren. This was the first time since Oklahoma statehood that [[Jackson County, Oklahoma|Jackson]], [[Stephens County, Oklahoma|Stephens]], and [[Grady County, Oklahoma|Grady]] counties voted Republican in a gubernatorial election, and the first time since 1914 that [[Comanche County, Oklahoma|Comanche]] county voted Republican. ==Primary election== Primary elections were held on August 23, 1994 with runoffs occurring on September 20, 1994. ===Democratic party=== Lt. Governor [[Jack Mildren]] and [[Bernice Shedrick]] advanced to the runoff where both candidates received vote totals similar to the first primary, securing the win for Mildren. ====Candidates====
